subject: Data-fence declaration & PrivateLink checksheet
messages:
From: Elena Park <epark@healthcore.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthCore Compliance <compliance@healthcore.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:14:00-05:00
Subject: Data residency & peering (data-fence) — docs needed

Hi Logan,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our procurement loop I need two items to continue: a short, signed "data-fence" declaration that confirms (1) tenant compute and storage for our account will remain in the EU region (single-country preference: Germany), and (2) that VPC/PrivateLink connections will not traverse the public internet (privatelink/privatelink peering or direct connect equivalent).

Separately we need an excerpted ops checklist listing private endpoint IP ranges, expected egress NAT behavior, and whether you can provide a customer-managed KMS partition (separate keys for our tenant). We have SIG/CAIQ reviews in progress — if you can attach a working draft of SIG answers and the CAIQ-relevant runbook that'd be helpful.

Target timeline: please get back by COB Tuesday (we're running an internal risk review Wednesday). If there's any policy text we need to sign or a DocuSign link, send it over.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Senior Compliance Manager
HealthCore

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <epark@healthcore.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T11:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Data residency & peering (data-fence) — docs needed

Elena — thanks for the clear list. High level answers up front then attachments and next steps below.

Short answers:
- Region & residency: We can pin your account to the EU-Germany zone and enforce compute & object storage residency for production workloads.
- Private connectivity: We support PrivateLink + dedicated peering. All traffic to model inference nodes for your tenant will traverse private peering or AWS PrivateLink endpoints; we will not route inference traffic over the public internet in production.
- KMS: We can support a customer-managed KMS in your AWS account (BYOK) or provide tenant-isolated keys in our managed HSM with a separate key partition per customer.

Attached: 1) data-fence-declaration-v1.pdf — a one-page commitment draft you can attach to your risk packet, 2) privatelink-ip-range-checksheet.xlsx — proposed endpoint IPs and CIDR suggestions for peering, 3) sig-answers-draft.docx — draft SIG/CAIQ responses we typically provide for this profile.

Operational notes / caveats:
- Failover: We can provision a hot-standby in eu-west as part of a DR plan but the active cluster will remain in eu-central (DE) by default; failover would be a controlled operation and documented in the runbook.
- Egress: By default we do not perform cross-border egress for inference payloads. If you enable telemetry forwarding to a HealthCore SaaS endpoint outside the EU, that will be an explicit opt-in combined with consent steps.
- Timeline: We can produce a signed data-fence letter and the final SIG answers within 3 business days once KMS choice is confirmed.

Next steps we need from you (short list):
1) Confirm whether you want BYOK in your account or managed HSM with tenant partition.
2) Confirm required single-country constraint (DE only) vs. EU-only acceptable.
3) Provide preferred window for peering cutover (we'll need a one-hour maintenance window).

Irene, can you pick this up for runbook details (peering config + NAT/egress behavior) and attach the ops excerpt? Marissa, can you shepherd the SIG answers to final?

I'll send the DocuSign link for the one-page data-fence after we agree on the KMS model.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Park <epark@healthcore.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthCore Compliance <compliance@healthcore.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T13:27:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Data residency & peering (data-fence) — docs needed

Thanks Logan — quick clarifications from our side (we're in CET):
- HealthCore requires single-country residency; Germany required for production.
- BYOK preferred (our security team wants keys in our account). If that is possible, please include the exact IAM policies and trust conditions we need to attach to our KMS key.
- For peering: we need the IP ranges for ACLs and the expected source port translations so our network team can pre-stage firewall rules.

Two quick asks:
1) Can you call out explicitly in the data-fence letter that model logs and temporary inference caches will not be replicated outside Germany? (We can live with product telemetry metadata forwarded to a telemetry collector in EU if necessary.)
2) Do you accept DocuSign signature for the one-pager? If yes, please send.

We want to keep the procurement timeline — internal risk sign-off on Wednesday morning. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Regards,
Elena

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <epark@healthcore.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T16:42:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Data residency & peering (data-fence) — docs needed

Elena — great, all doable. Summary of commitments and the deliverables we attached/linked: 

Commitments (short):
- Production compute, model weights, inference caches, and logs for your tenant will be provisioned in eu-central-1 (Germany) and will not be replicated outside the country unless you request specific archive/export actions.
- PrivateLink/peering only for inference traffic in production. No public internet traversal.
- BYOK supported. We'll provide an IAM trust policy snippet and the minimal key policy for your KMS key; your security team will keep the key in your account.

Deliverables attached/included:
- data-fence-declaration-v1.pdf (attached) — updated to explicitly call out logs & temporary caches.
- privatelink-ip-range-checksheet.xlsx (attached) — includes: private endpoint IPs, recommended CIDRs for peering, NAT behavior notes, and suggested firewall rules.
- sig-answers-draft.docx (attached) — Marissa will finalize the SIG answers and mark any questions that need procurement/legal review.
- Ops excerpt (inline below) — Irene included the critical ops excerpts for NAT/egress gating.

Irene's ops excerpt (high level):
- Private endpoints: we will provision elastic ENIs in the peering VPC using customer-assigned CIDRs. Suggested ACLs: allow TCP 443 inbound from HealthCore CIDR; block 0.0.0.0/0 inbound.
- NAT/Egress behavior: all outbound maintenance/patching traffic originates from a dedicated NAT gateway per tenant inside the eu-central management VPC; we will annotate flows in our audit logs with your tenant id.
- KMS BYOK flow: Redwood will perform a cross-account grant during provisioning; your account retains key ownership and rotation controls. We will not retain key material.

DocuSign: https://app.redwood.com/docusign/HC-2026-11-12 (link above) — I'm sending the one-pager there now for signature.

Marissa, please attach the finalized SIG answers and mark any items that need legal redlines. Irene, let's produce a one-page ops runbook excerpt and hand it to HealthCore's network team before their pre-staging window tomorrow.

We'll aim to have the signed data-fence and final SIG patch by Tuesday EOD CET.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachments: data-fence-declaration-v1.pdf (1 page), privatelink-ip-range-checksheet.xlsx (3 tabs), sig-answers-draft.docx (working draft)
